title: Freelance sessions while on staff, including the unreleased Billie Holiday Story
summary: He played sessions with Red Allen, Max Kaminsky, Hackett, Armstrong and others, and later played on Chaney Scott's Billie Holiday Story, withheld after a lawsuit, around 1960.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now

blocks.x: Then in the meantime in the radio station you had other opportunities to play other places. And I played, you know, with every -- all of the sessions and things that were around. Then I did some work with -- I played with Red Allen. I was with Red Allen quite a bit. We played Max Kamansky and Bobby Hackett. And meanwhile Coleman Hawkins and Wilbur deParis and Louis Armstrong. And the Dukes of Dixieland, Roy Eldridge --

No, this is during that time after, see. And the Dukes of Dixieland, Roy Eldridge, Lionel Hampton, and then I did a record for Chaney Scott, did the thing called the Billie Holiday Story. They didn't release that because the Billie Holiday Foundation or whatever it was put a suit in and the record wasn't released. But he was in there.
Oh, heck, this was done around 1960 or so.
